title: Etekcity Digital Kitchen Scale Review: Accurate and Easy to Clean
metaDescription: Testing the Etekcity stainless steel kitchen scale for accuracy, durability, and daily cooking needs. Real user experience after weeks of use.
content:
## Build Quality That Actually Lasts

The 304 stainless steel surface caught my attention immediately - it's not just for looks. After spilling everything from flour to sticky honey on this scale, cleanup takes seconds with a damp cloth. The platform feels substantial underfoot, not flimsy like some cheaper models I've used. The LCD display sits at just the right angle for reading without craning your neck.

## Accuracy Where It Counts

I tested this against my old mechanical scale using various ingredients. Measuring out 100 grams of flour, 50 grams of butter, and 200 grams of sugar showed consistent readings within a gram or two. The tare function works instantly - no waiting around for it to reset when you add a new bowl. Switch between grams and ounces with one button press, which comes in handy when following recipes from different sources.

The scale responds quickly to weight changes. Add ingredients gradually and you'll see the numbers climb in real-time without lag. It's sensitive enough to register a single almond but stable enough that minor vibrations won't throw off your measurements.

## Daily Use Reality Check

After using this for meal prep and regular cooking, a few things stand out. The platform size handles most mixing bowls comfortably - I can fit my 2-quart glass bowl with room to spare. The maximum weight capacity covers everything I've needed for batch cooking and portioning.

Battery life has been solid. I use it several times a week and haven't needed to replace the batteries yet after two months. The auto-shutoff kicks in after about two minutes of inactivity, which helps preserve power.

## Minor Frustrations

The buttons are flush with the surface, which looks sleek but can be hard to press when your hands are wet or covered in flour. Sometimes it takes a couple tries to register the press. The display, while clear, could be slightly larger for easier reading in dim kitchen lighting.

The scale occasionally takes a second or two longer to stabilize when measuring very light items like herbs or spices. Not a dealbreaker, but noticeable when you're trying to work quickly.

## Who This Works Best For

If you do regular baking, meal prep, or follow recipes that use weight measurements, this scale handles the job reliably. The stainless steel surface makes it ideal for messy cooking projects since cleanup is so straightforward. It's compact enough for smaller kitchens but substantial enough to feel professional.

For casual cooks who only occasionally need precise measurements, it might be overkill. But if you're serious about consistent results in your cooking, the accuracy and durability justify the investment.
pros: 304 stainless steel surface cleans effortlessly with just a damp cloth
Accurate measurements within 1-2 grams across different ingredient types
Instant tare function with no waiting time between measurements
Quick response time shows weight changes in real-time without lag
Platform size accommodates most standard mixing bowls comfortably
Battery life lasts months with regular several-times-weekly use
Auto-shutoff after 2 minutes helps preserve battery power
cons: Flush buttons can be difficult to press with wet or flour-covered hands
Display could be larger for easier reading in dim kitchen lighting
Takes slightly longer to stabilize when weighing very light items like herbs
Buttons sometimes require multiple presses to register properly
verdict: This scale delivers reliable accuracy and easy maintenance for regular cooking and baking needs. The stainless steel surface and solid build quality make it a practical long-term kitchen tool, despite minor button design issues.
targetAudience: Home bakers, meal preppers, and serious cooks who need consistent weight measurements for recipes and portion control
